Anna Wu: Heads-up — ran parity tests across AWS/GCP/Azure for A100-80GB-equivalent. Throughput close but p95 latency diverges depending on driver/CUDA stack. Chart: https://redwood.internal/charts/cross-cloud-a100-2026 :bar_chart:
Dmitri Petrov: Nice. Which instance SKUs and driver/CUDA combos did you test?
Anna Wu: Setup details:
- AWS: p4d.24xlarge, NVIDIA driver 525.60, CUDA 11.8, cuDNN 8.5
- GCP: a2-megagpu-16g, NVIDIA driver 510.47, CUDA 11.8, cuDNN 8.4
- Azure: ND96asr_v4, NVIDIA driver 470.129, CUDA 11.0, cuDNN 8.0.5
All runs used the same model binary (gpt-compat-v3), identical compilation flags and our quant hook for int8.
Samir Patel: Workload details? seq len, batch, precision?
Anna Wu: Test matrix:
- seq_len: 1536 (prompt 256 + gen 512)
- batch sizes: 1,2,4
- precisions: fp16 baseline, GPTQ-style int8 simulated
Key aggregated numbers (tokens/sec; p50 / p95 latency ms), rounded:
AWS/us-west-2: bs1 1100 tps, p50 90ms, p95 230ms; bs4 3600 tps, p50 240ms, p95 520ms
GCP/us-central1: bs1 1200 tps, p50 82ms, p95 180ms; bs4 3900 tps, p50 210ms, p95 410ms
Azure/eastus: bs1 900 tps, p50 110ms, p95 340ms; bs4 3000 tps, p50 280ms, p95 650ms
Int8 upsides: ~+18-22% tokens/sec on AWS/GCP, only ~+6-9% on Azure.
Dmitri Petrov: That's a pretty consistent pattern. Do you have kernel-selection logs? suspect fallback kernels on the older CUDA/drivers.
Anna Wu: Yes, runtime kernel selection shows different paths. Snippet:
```
[serve] selected_kernel=matmul_cutlass_fused, workspace=1.8GB, path=fast
[serve] selected_kernel=kv_cache_cublaslt, path=fast
[serve] selected_kernel=matmul_cublas_legacy, path=slow  # observed on azure nodes
[serve] memcpy(extra_copy)=0.12ms  # per chunk, higher on azure
```
Maria Gonzalez: Did you try pushing a newer driver on Azure to see if perf aligns?
Anna Wu: I deployed a preview image with driver 510.79 on a small ND96 test cluster. Result: p95 improved ~60ms for bs1 and bs4; int8 gains matched the others. But that required manual driver install + reboot and isn't available in our default subscription images.
Samir Patel: Do the CSVs show where time is spent? memcopy vs compute?
Anna Wu: Yes — full CSV attached to the bench job. Quick summary: memcpy/copy stalls accounted for ~10-15% of latency on Azure for bs4, vs ~2-4% on AWS/GCP. Also saw more kernel retries on Azure leading to tail spikes.
Dmitri Petrov: Could topology/NVLINK differences explain the extra copies?
Anna Wu: Exactly. AWS/GCP instances had full NVLINK interconnect between all GPUs in the host. The Azure SKU we hit had non-uniform peer access (some pairs over PCIe), so the runtime inserted extra copies and fell back to older matmul kernels.
BenchBot: Benchmark job 1763601175 finished. CSV: https://redwood.internal/bench/1763601175.csv
Maria Gonzalez: Actionable items?
Anna Wu: Proposed next steps:
- Infra: run automated driver matrix (470 / 510 / 525) across the three providers on same SKU and collect kernel-selection logs + NVLINK topology. (assigned: infra)
- Eng-ML: run int8 quality/regression eval on the Azure 510 driver image before recommending it broadly. (assigned: eng-ml)
- Product/Docs: add a region/provider note about driver/CUDA impact and recommended images for Dedicated/Private deployments.
Samir Patel: I'll queue the matrix runs and link outputs to the bench CSV. Also adding infra note: for Azure Dedicated recommendations include a custom driver rollout path.
Anna Wu: I'll draft a short RFC with perf snapshots, runbook, and reproduction commands. Repro command we used:
```
docker run --gpus all \n  -e MODEL_TAG=gpt-compat-v3 \n  -e CUDA_VERBOSE_KERNEL_SELECTION=1 \n  --cpus 16 --memory 120g \n  redwood/serve:bench-2026-03-21 \n  --batches 1,2,4 --seq 1536 --quant int8,fp16 --iters 250
```
BenchBot: tagging @Infra for the driver matrix run.
